Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 55, verses 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Rahman (the Most Merciful), because it opens with this name from among the Beautiful Names of Allah, and the surah repeatedly reminds of Allah's many blessings, and these blessings go back to the meaning of this noble name.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Mention of a number of Allah's blessings and His striking signs, which are evident in His beautiful creation, His wondrous making of creation, and His management of existence, all of which are among the effects of Allah's mercy that He has bestowed upon His servants; as a reminder to them of the duty of gratitude.

• A threat and warning to the jinn and mankind, as a preparation for the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the reckoning that will take place on it, and mention of what will follow after that, the punishment of the wretched and the bliss of the blessed.

[The Tafsir]

﴿The Most Merciful taught the Qur'an.﴾ Through facilitating its recitation, its memorization, and the understanding of its meanings.

And the sky He raised high above the earth, and He placed in the earth the justice that He commanded and prescribed for His servants.

Then which of the favors of your Lord, both the religious and the worldly, do you two (O assembly of jinn and mankind) deny?

And how excellent was the response of the jinn when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this surah to them: whenever he came to this verse, they would say: "We deny none of Your bounties, our Lord; to You be all praise." Likewise, when the favors and bounties of Allah are recited to a servant, he should acknowledge them, thank Allah, and praise Him for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 55, verse 16:

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ O assembly of jinn and humankind, which of your Lord's blessings do you deny?
He, glorified and exalted is He, is the Lord of the two risings of the sun, in winter and in summer, and the Lord of its two settings in them. So all of creation is under His management and lordship.
Then which of the favors of your Lord, O two worlds (jinn and humankind), will you deny?

God mingled the two seas, the sweet and the salty, so that they meet, with no barrier visible to the eye between them. Yet between them there is a barrier, so neither overpowers the other and eliminates its properties. Rather, the sweet remains sweet and the salty remains salty even though they meet.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 55, verse 26–27:

Everyone on the earth among the creation will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Bounty. ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, but there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.﴾ In the verse is the affirmation of the attribute of Face for Allah, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting Him, without likening (tashbih) Him to creation and without specifying a modality (takyif) for it.
